resumeLine: Built a durable job queue on PostgreSQL processing ~10k jobs/day with lease-based worker recovery.

claims.quote: Built a durable job queue on PostgreSQL processing ~10k jobs/day

answers.text: We claim a job by setting lease_until thirty seconds ahead in the same update that selects it, so two workers can never take the same row. If the worker dies the lease expires and another picks it up.
It retries. If a worker dies the job gets picked up again.
We used the standard approach for that.

The lease is the recovery mechanism: a dead worker's job becomes claimable again once lease_until passes. What we never handled is the resurrected worker completing the job a second time — completeJob checks nothing.
Lease-based recovery. The lease expires and the work continues.

seededDefects.description: A resurrected worker whose lease expired mid-job can complete the job a second time; completeJob checks nothing.
The worker never extends its lease, so any job slower than the 30s lease is silently reassigned.
